transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-03
Start: 15:30 PDT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Luis Ortega (Redwood CSM), Dr. Elena Cruz (Ionova Head of ML), Samir Rao (Ionova CTO), Kara Lee (Ionova Procurement)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be brief): Discussed short-term contract bridge, Dedicated capacity uplift for inference, EU VPC onboarding, security checklist (SOC2/KMS), and next steps for benchmarks and PO timing.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Jordan (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for coming on, appreciate you carving out time. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Dr. Elena Cruz: Hi Elena here.
[00:07] Samir Rao: Samir.
[00:09] Kara Lee: Kara.
[00:11] Maya (SE): Maya from Redwood. Luis in chat as well.
[00:14] Jordan: Cool. We put a short agenda in the invite: bridge contract, capacity uplift, EU VPC plan and security. We'll jump in.
[01:02] Samir: Quick context — we're at about 350k inference tokens/day right now, spiky e‑commerce surge nights push to 1.2M tokens. We're approaching your renewal in mid-October and procurement wants a clear ramp plan.
[01:28] Dr. Elena: Also we have regulatory work in EU — need VPC and KMS, plus longer retention of audit logs.
[01:35] Jordan: Totally. So two asks from our side before we propose: one, would you consider a 12-month bridge to lock current rates while you finish procurement? Two, what's the desired capacity uplift and when do you want EU VPC online?
[01:54] Samir: For bridge— yes, procurement wants that option. For capacity we want Dedicated + burst capacity to handle the 1.2M spikes with headroom, target go‑live for EU VPC by end of November.
[02:15] Maya: Can I ask about QPS shape — are the spikes short bursts or multi-hour? That affects batching and kernel selection.
[02:25] Samir: Short bursts, often 5–20 mins, but can hit ten concurrent long‑running streams during batch jobs.
[02:34] Maya: Got it. That's helpful for autoscale policy suggestions — continuous batching helps but for 5–20 min spikes we recommend a burst pool + prewarming.
[03:02] Dr. Elena: On security: SOC2 in place, but we need KMS integration with our Azure Key Vault/HSM. Is that supported on the Private / VPC deployment?
[03:12] Luis (CSM): Yes, Private supports KMS and HSM integrations; we'll outline supported KMS providers in the runbook.
[03:21] Kara: Also need data residency: logs and audit trail retained for 7 years for compliance.
[03:30] Jordan: We can configure audit retention and export to your SIEM; that'll be in scope for Private deployments. We'll confirm retention SLAs.
[03:55] Samir: Pricing question — if we do a 12‑month bridge, does that preserve current committed rates and give us time to finalize EU private onboarding?
[04:03] Jordan: Yes, bridge is priced as a short commitment at current rates but with a smaller minimum. Think of it as 50% of your expected commit for 12 months, and then you can convert credits on renewal. We'll send numbers.
[04:18] Dr. Elena: Are there tech caveats if we convert from hosted to Private Dedicated mid-contract?
[04:25] Maya: There's a migration path — same API surface, but model variants and quantization profiles may differ slightly. We support model pins and controlled rollouts so you can validate outputs. There's also KV cache behavior — that moves with the model, but we capture prefix caches where possible.
[04:52] Samir: Latency target — we need p95 < 220ms for the 512 token case. Can Redwood meet that in EU region on your Dedicated nodes?
[05:02] Maya: On typical configs, yes. We'll run a targeted benchmark with your sample traces to validate p95 and suggest instance types and quantization.
[05:15] Jordan: We'll include a benchmark plan as a Deliverable.
[05:25] Kara: Procurement timeline — if we sign a bridge by Sept 15, can we push EU onboarding timeline to Nov 30? We need time to approve network peering.
[05:34] Jordan: That timeline is feasible; the critical path is getting network CIDR and firewall exceptions for the peering. Maya will list the exact ports and CIDRs.
[06:02] Maya: On networking, we need a transit gateway or classic VPC peering depending on your cloud. We also support private link in Azure for lower surface area.
[06:17] Samir: We run mostly on Azure in EU-West; private link would be preferable.
[06:24] Maya: Okay we'll note Azure Private Link and sample ARM templates.
[06:40] (short crosstalk)
[07:02] Dr. Elena: A question about model fallbacks — if the Dedicated pool is saturated do you have graceful fallback to a smaller hosted model so user experience degrades but stays up?
[07:12] Maya: Yes, we can set routing policies for fallback to a cheaper/compatible model. You can configure by route: latency SLO vs cost SLO.
[07:25] Samir: Good. We'll need that — can't have downtime during campaigns.
[07:33] Jordan: One other note — auditability for ML outputs, you mentioned retention of prompts and responses for some workflows. We can add data masking policies and configurable retention per route.
[07:45] Dr. Elena: We'll need masking for PHI patterns before storing in logs.
[07:50] Maya: We have pre-store scrubbing hooks and configurable regex masking; we'll include examples.
[08:12] Kara: On procurement, if we sign bridge and then convert to a 24-month commitment in January, how do credits or overages settle?
[08:21] Jordan: We typically convert unused bridge credit towards the new commit; overage during bridge is billed at agreed overage rates. We'll put concrete examples in the quote.
[08:34] Samir: For the Dedicated capacity, what's the lead time for provisioning EU nodes if we pick a specific GPU profile?
[08:42] Maya: Typical provisioning is 3–5 weeks for Dedicated pools; with prioritized provisioning we can target 2 weeks but would need an explicit PO and deposit.
[08:55] Dr. Elena: That matters — if we want Nov 30 go‑live, we probably need to approve PO by end of Sept.
[09:04] Jordan: Understood. So action item: Jordan to send the 12‑month bridge quote by Sept 10. Maya will follow with the EU VPC runbook & port list by Sept 12. Elena to provide latency traces by Sept 17. Kara to confirm procurement timeline by Sept 15.
[09:32] (pause)
[10:02] Samir: On the technical deep dive — we might need an SE-led bench next week. Can Maya run a bench against our sample payloads?
[10:10] Maya: Yes. If you share sample traces and a small test key we can run a dedicated benchmark and return p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens.
[10:24] Dr. Elena: We'll sanitize traces — but want realistic spike behavior included.
[10:30] Maya: Perfect. We also will include quantization options and expected accuracy delta; you can pick FP16 vs 4-bit quant.
[10:40] Samir: Accuracy delta matters for clinical gating. We'll want to validate OOT (out-of-time) sample set.
[10:47] Maya: We'll include evaluation harness suggestions.
[11:03] Jordan: Quick question from procurement: will Redwood require a data processing addendum for the VPC deployment?
[11:10] Luis: We have a DPA template for EU customers; we'll attach it and the SOC2 attestation.
[11:20] Kara: Great, please send that. Also need software escrow details?
[11:25] Jordan: For Private deployments we can discuss escrow as part of enterprise package; we'll flag that to legal.
[11:35] (filler, some background noise)
[12:02] Dr. Elena: Regarding KV cache — we saw some mismatch on previous PoC where prefix caching didn't persist across restarts. Any update?
[12:12] Maya: We improved persistence in last runtime release; persistence should hold across scheduled restarts, but we'll validate with your workload. There may be edge cases with preemption on burst pools.
[12:28] Samir: Ok we need that validation.
[12:34] Jordan: We'll add the cache validation to the benchmark scope.
[13:00] (short silence)
[13:32] Jordan: Rundown — items and dates (reads action items). Any other questions?
[13:40] Samir: One more — region parity. Will EU nodes support the same model catalog as Hosted US?
[13:48] Maya: Most open models and verified variants will be available; some proprietary tuned variants won't be in Private by default but we can onboard model binaries as part of the Dedicated plan.
[14:05] Dr. Elena: Good to know.
[14:10] Kara: Ok thanks, expecting docs and quote this week.
[14:15] Jordan: We'll aim to get documents first thing. Thanks everyone.
[47:10] End of recording (note: timestamps pasted roughly; transcript truncated to key parts).
